draft.title: Combining transformations
card: In y = kf(a(x + b)) + c, the numbers a and b change x. The numbers k and c change y. A negative a reflects in the y-axis. A negative k reflects in the x-axis.
Do dilations and reflections first, then translations. A point (x, y) on y = f(x) moves to (x/a − b, ky + c).
The x-coordinate is divided by a, not multiplied. Then b is taken away, so x + b shifts the graph left by b.
Example: (6, 3) is on y = f(x). On y = 2f(3(x − 1)) + 4, x becomes 6 ÷ 3 = 2, then 2 + 1 = 3. y becomes 2 × 3 = 6, then 6 + 4 = 10. The new point is (3, 10).
draft.remember: Dilate and reflect first, then translate. The x-coordinate is divided by a.

a.q: The point (4, −2) is on y = f(x). What is its image on y = −f(2x) + 1?
a.why: x becomes 4 ÷ 2 = 2. For y, reflect first to get 2, then add 1 to get 3. (2, 1) is wrong because it adds 1 before reflecting, which is the wrong order.
a.clue: Reflect and dilate before you translate.

b.q: The point (6, 2) is on y = f(x). What is its image on y = 3f(½(x + 1)) − 4?
b.why: Dividing x by ½ gives 12. Then x + 1 shifts the graph left by 1, so x becomes 11. For y, 3 × 2 = 6, then 6 − 4 = 2. (13, 2) is wrong because it shifts right instead of left.
b.clue: Dividing by ½ is the same as doubling, and + 1 inside the bracket moves left.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's rule and worked example are correct, and both questions have exactly one right answer, (2, 3) and (11, 2), which match the explanations.

final.title: Combining transformations
card: In \(y = kf(a(x + b)) + c\), the numbers \(a\) and \(b\) change \(x\). The numbers \(k\) and \(c\) change \(y\). A negative \(a\) reflects in the y-axis. A negative \(k\) reflects in the x-axis.
Do dilations and reflections first, then translations. A point \((x, y)\) on \(y = f(x)\) moves to \((\frac{x}{a} - b, ky + c)\).
The x-coordinate is divided by \(a\), not multiplied. Then \(b\) is taken away, so \(x + b\) shifts the graph left by \(b\).

Example: \((6, 3)\) is on \(y = f(x)\). On \(y = 2f(3(x - 1)) + 4\), \(x\) becomes \(6 \div 3 = 2\), then \(2 + 1 = 3\). \(y\) becomes \(2 \times 3 = 6\), then \(6 + 4 = 10\). The new point is \((3, 10)\).
final.remember: Dilate and reflect first, then translate. The x-coordinate is divided by \(a\).

a.q: The point \((4, -2)\) is on \(y = f(x)\). What is its image on \(y = -f(2x) + 1\)?
a.why: \(x\) becomes \(4 \div 2 = 2\). For \(y\), reflect first to get 2, then add 1 to get 3. \((2, 1)\) is wrong because it adds 1 before reflecting, which is the wrong order.
a.clue: Reflect and dilate before you translate.

b.q: The point \((6, 2)\) is on \(y = f(x)\). What is its image on \(y = 3f(\frac{1}{2}(x + 1)) - 4\)?
b.why: Dividing \(x\) by \(\frac{1}{2}\) gives 12. Then \(x + 1\) shifts the graph left by 1, so \(x\) becomes 11. For \(y\), \(3 \times 2 = 6\), then \(6 - 4 = 2\). \((13, 2)\) is wrong because it shifts right instead of left.
b.clue: Dividing by \(\frac{1}{2}\) is the same as doubling, and \(+1\) inside the bracket moves left.

wants.brief: The dashed curve y = f(x) with f(x) = x^2/12 (fn \frac{x^{2}}{12}) and the solid curve y = 2f(3(x - 1)) + 4, which is 1.5(x - 1)^2 + 4, both labelled. Mark (6, 3) on f and its image (3, 10) on the new curve, with an arrow from (6, 3) to (3, 10). Axes x from -2 to 8 and y from 0 to 12.
wants.why: It shows the point moving left and up as card line 4 works out.
